verdict.rationale: Phoenix documents running operations over many items at once in the evaluation and experiment context. It can run thousands of evaluations with built-in concurrency and retry handling, and it can rerun grouped traces as datasets through new application versions. There is no evidence of general-purpose bulk actions on traces, spans, datasets, prompts or annotations, such as bulk delete, bulk tag/label, bulk export or multi-select edits. missing for 10: general bulk edit/delete/annotate operations across traces or dataset items, bulk operations exposed via API/CLI/MCP, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: This means you can run thousands of evaluations without writing any retry or concurrency logic yourself.
You can group traces into datasets, rerun them through different versions of your application, and compare evaluation results
You can run evaluations on traces from production, on experiment results, or on any dataset.
